The continuation could not be written locally: the workspace rejected read-only shell access before repository inspection, so I could not update `research-ledger-manifest.json` or verify the notebook. I’m not claiming those changes were made.

I completed a bounded continuation for selected chapter 1B and recovered these append-ready units, preserving the stated lens mappings:

- `WEB-1B-016`: Bundestag budget records placed F-35 procurement in the 2023 “Dimension Luft” budget, with €635.1m expenditure and €8.81bn commitment authority. Supports `1B.3`, `1B.10`; contrary: funding confirms implementation, not safety or risk reduction. [Bundestag budget record](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-920662)

- `WEB-1B-017`: SIPRI describes umbrella states as balancing alliance commitments requiring support for nuclear deterrence against disarmament norms; this directly contextualizes Germany’s inherited nuclear-sharing posture. Supports `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.10`; attribution: indirect. [SIPRI analysis](https://www.sipri.org/publications/2023/sipri-insights-peace-and-security/role-umbrella-states-global-nuclear-order)

- `WEB-1B-018`: ICAN argued that nuclear sharing conflicts with TPNW obligations and creates humanitarian and proliferation risks. Supports `1B.3`, `1B.5`, `1B.10`; attribution: contrary civil-society assessment, not an adjudicated legal finding. [ICAN statement](https://www.icanw.de/neuigkeiten/npt23-ican-erklaerung-zur-nuklearen-teilhabe/)

- `WEB-1B-019`: Germany’s February 2023 Conference on Disarmament statement linked arms control with deterrence, called for escalation-risk reduction, and warned that autonomous weapons must remain under human control. Supports `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.9`; contrary: policy position without implementation proof. [Federal Foreign Office speech](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom/news/baerbock-disarmament-conference-2584526)

- `WEB-1B-020`: Germany’s May 2023 CCW statement supported prohibiting fully autonomous lethal weapons and requiring concrete human-control provisions across the weapons lifecycle. Supports `1B.9`, `1B.1`; attribution: government-level, not personally Scholz-specific. [German national statement](https://docs-library.unoda.org/Convention_on_Certain_Conventional_Weapons_-Group_of_Governmental_Experts_on_Lethal_Autonomous_Weapons_Systems_%282023%29/230515_%28DEU_Statement%29_LAWS_GGE_delivered.pdf)

- `WEB-1B-021`: Germany’s July 2023 NPT PrepCom statement reaffirmed the NPT, criticized nuclear threats and treaty erosion, defended NATO nuclear sharing as NPT-consistent, and supported CTBT entry into force and IAEA verification. Supports `1B.2`, `1B.4`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`; contrary: the same record confirms continued reliance on nuclear sharing. [German NPT statement](https://docs-library.unoda.org/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons_-Preparatory_Committee_for_the_Eleventh_Review_ConferenceFirst_session_%282023%29/Germany_Final__GD.pdf)

No score or ranking was assigned. The principal unresolved gap remains independent evidence of actual nuclear-risk outcomes, safety implementation, and direct Scholz-level responsibility.
